value.body: An editor reviews and improves written content for accuracy, clarity, structure and style before it is published. Employers include publishing houses, newspapers and digital media, content and edtech companies, and corporate communications teams. A typical day involves editing drafts, checking facts, working with writers on revisions and meeting publication deadlines.

items.value: B.A. English, Journalism or Mass Communication

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers often start as copy editors, sub-editors, proofreaders or editorial assistants, usually after an editing test. Prior writing work and internships at publications help.

value.title: At a glance
items: Many editors begin as writers or proofreaders.
Next roles: senior editor, managing editor, commissioning editor.
Print roles have shrunk; digital and corporate editing have grown.
